summary: Gone Bald Mountain tower in Craig County, VA: FFLOS dates it to 1955 and removal to about 2000-2002, while a CCC account describes a 1940 tower there.

facts.design: Wood cab on a 40-foot tower, per the April 1940 CCC account
facts.status_note: Removed about 2000-2002; no source describes the site today

events.note: CCC company entry dated April 1940 says a 40-foot tower with a wood cab was completed April 20; does not match the 1955 listing
FFLOS build date; one of two Craig County towers built that year

evidence.supports: tower built 1955 as one of two Craig County towers; overlooked New Castle to the south
evidence.quote: One of two towers built in Craig County in 1955, Bald Mountain overlooked New Castle to the south.

evidence.supports: site in the Jefferson National Forest, Craig County
other tower in the county was on Potts Mountain
evidence.quote: Bald Mountain runs parallel to Potts Mountain, the other mountain that was home to a tower in this county.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
listing is the only account of the site; says nothing about the site today (no remains or access described)
evidence.quote: One of two towers built in Craig County in 1955, Bald Mountain overlooked New Castle to the south.

evidence.supports: CCC excavation began in September; structure not finished until April 20; entry dated April 1940
evidence.quote: began excavation for the erection of Bald Mountain Tower. However, due to inclement weather, the structure was not completed until April 20th.

evidence.supports: April 1940 date of the CCC entry
tower 40 feet tall with a 15 x 14 foot wood cab
evidence.quote: This new tower is a 40' structure including a 15' x 14' wood cab

evidence.supports: lookout to live in the cab during spring and fall fire seasons
evidence.quote: The lookout man will live in the cab, approximately 40' from the ground, during spring and fall fire seasons.

evidence.supports: 40,000 acres watched, in Craig, Alleghany and Botetourt counties (30,000 of them National Forest Land)
evidence.quote: He will be able to keep a clear and constant watch over 40,000 acres, of which 30,000 acres is National Forest Land, in Craig, Alleghany and Botetourt counties.

evidence.supports: excavation began in September (the entry reads 'During September')
evidence.quote: During September, enrollees of Camp F-21, under the supervision of Superintendent E.C. Hatcher, Foremen Humphreys and Shepherd and Engineer J.E. Junkin, began excavation for the erection of Bald Mountain Tower.

evidence.supports: 1955 listing date, which the 1940 CCC account does not match
evidence.quote: One of two towers built in Craig County in 1955

evidence.supports: second list marks the Craig County site as gone
evidence.quote: Bald Mountain Craig 37.61496 -80.03707 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1724, VA 26

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS dates the tower to 1955; a CCC company entry dated April 1940 describes a 40-foot tower on Bald Mountain. Neither source says whether the two are the same structure, so the story reports both dates.

notes_for_editor: Brief record matches FFLOS on coordinates, 1955 build, USFS administration and circa 2000-2002 removal; no correction needed. Gap: no source describes what remains on the summit or whether the site is open. The CCC account is read from a third-party transcription credited to 'Bob Cat - CCC Company 1368'; the April 1940 year comes from the entry heading, so the original newsletter would settle it. A search for the 1955 construction turned up nothing new. The Washington State Bald Mountain pages in search results are a different site and were ignored.
